title: Yankees’ Aaron Judge ‘making progress,’ ‘doing a lot of convincing’ ahead of Game 1
content:
NEW YORK — Aaron Judge has one final chance to convince the New York Yankees that he’s ready to play in the Wild Card Series.

Judge will participate in batting practice early Monday evening to see if he could be an option for the Yankees in the best-of-three set against the Boston Red Sox that begins Tuesday night.

“I’m going to see how (Monday) goes and then give them all of the input I can, and I think they’re going to use their eyes and talk with some people to see what’s probably best,” Judge said inside the Yankees’ clubhouse on Monday.

Judge has done hitting and running behind the scenes over the past few days, but he has not run the bases. Running the bases is usually standard protocol for a player rehabbing from a lower-body injury before they are activated. Judge said he could do some outdoor running Monday, but it hadn’t been officially decided before he spoke to reporters. The only running he has done since straining his right calf was on a zero-gravity treadmill, which limits the weight a person puts on their legs.

Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Monday the club is continuing to evaluate Judge by listening to the training and medical staff to see whether it’s a realistic option that the superstar right fielder could play.

“I’ve been doing a lot of convincing,” Judge said. “I’m gonna keep doing that. I think the most important thing is just making sure that I’m healthy and ready to go for this long stretch. We’ve got another month of baseball to play. I want to be ready for the long run we’re going to go on for this next month. We’re all going to be smart. I think they all know I want to be out there, especially the first game.”

Judge, who went on the injured list on Sept. 19, said he’s part of “zero plans,” and acknowledged Boone and the front office will ultimately decide whether he is on the roster.

“I don’t make the roster,” Judge said. “I don’t make the team. I’m just doing everything I can to let them make the decision. I want to be out there. That’s what I’ve said every single time. I don’t know how else I can say it besides that.”

Boone announced last week that Judge suffered a “moderate” grade calf strain, which normally requires a several-week recovery process. But it’s clear that Judge is trying to beat the standard timeline to return to play.

“Guys take risks every single day,” Judge said. “I know a lot of guys in here are banged up and dealing with stuff. I understand the risks.”

Judge is one of a handful of players about whom the Yankees have not a roster decision. As of Monday afternoon, Boone said the Yankees were still weighing whether Giancarlo Stanton, Trent Grisham and Ryan Weathers, who are all recovering from various injuries, would be available.
